items.title: What does it mean for students if Canada joins the Erasmus+ exchange program?
items.author: Santiago Sánchez Arbouin
items.excerpt: Going on exchange to Europe could be the bridge to deepen transatlantic relations With increasing ties between Europe and Canada, Canadian students might be able to join the Erasmus exchange program. Graphic Aia Segal This article originally appeared in The Link Volume 47, Issue
items.leadExcerpt: In the United States-Canada trade war, it is tricky to define a “winning” side. However, Canada is developing a unique relationship with Europe, one that could help Canada gain inclusion in the Erasmus+ exchange program. Canadian universities currently manage their exchange programs directly through bilateral agreements between institutions. This limits not only student mobility but also the funding available for them.

items.title: Basketball has a flopping problem
items.author: Oliver Richman
items.excerpt: The NBA’s best players are resorting to acting instead of simply playing the game. Diving in the NBA needs to come to an end. Graphic by Dia Diekmann @diadrws
items.leadExcerpt: Drawing fouls is a big part of basketball. It is an art form in itself. But players are beginning to take it too far, embellishing and dramatically flopping on the court in hopes of a whistle. The worst part is, they are getting away with it. The referees do not care, and they are willing to blow the whistle at any sign that a star player is struggling to create space or score. Seeing it in the National Basketball Association (NBA), kids are starting to emulate it in their games as well. Their favourite players are throwing themselves on the ground, so why wouldn’t they?

items.title: Nostalgia Nook: Once upon a CD
items.author: Ikram Dridi
items.excerpt: Was the change from CD/ DVDs worth it? CDs and DVDs represent a time when we actually owned the media we paid for. Graphic Lola McCarthy This article originally appeared in The Link Volume 47, Issue 5, published November 10, 2026.
items.leadExcerpt: One of my favourite childhood memories is movie nights. Every Saturday, the whole family would gather around the TV with popcorn and hot chocolate, then choose a movie to watch from our CD/DVD binder. I have fond memories of going to the CD/DVD store with my parents. They would purchase any movie I found interesting, and we would spend evenings organizing the CDs in the binders by collection and genre. Technology became more advanced as I grew up. We discarded CDs and DVDs, and our big collection turned into arts-and-crafts projects. Now everything is on streaming subscription-based platforms. We pay more across platforms than what we did to build our collections, and we don’t even own the physical media anymore.

items.title: Goodbye October, Hello Movember!
items.author: Charlotte Cochrane
items.excerpt: With Halloween in the rearview mirror, Movember is officially upon us! Bishop’s University’s men’s rugby team is participating in this month-long event which raises funds for men’s health initiatives. The Movember website states that they’ve raised over
items.leadExcerpt: With Halloween in the rearview mirror, Movember is officially upon us! Bishop’s University’s men’s rugby team is participating in this month-long event which raises funds for men’s health initiatives. The Movember website states that they’ve raised over “$1.8 billion AUD in prevention-focused work across mental health and suicide prevention, prostate cancer and testicular cancer”, in the past 22 years, worldwide. Movember is the type of fundraiser that not only brings community and funds research, but also raises awareness regarding men’s health– something that is not nearly talked about enough.

items.title: The SCC is M.I.A.: A Symptom of a Bigger Extracurricular Issue at Bishop’s

items.excerpt: As we approach the time of year when Take Back the Night takes to the streets of Lennoxville as a student-led protest against sexual violence, the Sexual Culture Committee has been confirmed inactive by the SRC. After eight years of Take Back the Night, the failure to transition
items.leadExcerpt: As we approach the time of year when Take Back the Night takes to the streets of Lennoxville as a student-led protest against sexual violence, the Sexual Culture Committee has been confirmed inactive by the SRC. After eight years of Take Back the Night, the failure to transition executive teams has caused the unplanned hiatus of the SCC. With huge changes to the Sexual Violence Support Centre this year, including two new Sexual Violence Response Advisors, it is imperative to have at least one constant: a student-led, university-supported outlet and resource for students to refer to.

items.title: Sherbrooke to Enforce More Regulations on Parking in Lennoxville
items.author: Anthony Ouellet
items.excerpt: Do you think there’s a lot of free parking around campus? The City of Sherbrooke certainly does, and it is going to reduce the number of available on-street parking spaces in Lennoxville even more. Sherbrooke is planning to uniformize parking restrictions on Queen St., Speid
items.leadExcerpt: Do you think there’s a lot of free parking around campus? The City of Sherbrooke certainly does, and it is going to reduce the number of available on-street parking spaces in Lennoxville even more. Sherbrooke is planning to uniformize parking restrictions on Queen St., Speid St., Church St. and Samuel-Gratham St. While both Queen St. and Speid St. offer free, unrestricted parking spaces in Lennoxville, Church St. and Samuel-Gratham St. have restrictions ranging from 60 to 120 minutes.
